settings.cf_tunnel_desc: Monitor the live health status of your private Cloudflare Tunnel (cloudflared).
settings.cf_tunnel_guide_title: How to setup Cloudflare Zero Trust Tunnel Monitoring:
settings.cf_tunnel_step1_desc: Log in to the Cloudflare Dashboard. Choose any domain or check your browser address bar: https://dash.cloudflare.com/<ACCOUNT_ID>. Alternatively, on any domain Overview page, scroll down the right sidebar to copy the 32-character Account ID.
settings.cf_tunnel_step2_desc: Open the Zero Trust Dashboard -> Networks -> Tunnels. Select your active tunnel. The Tunnel ID (UUID format xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx) is displayed in the tunnel overview and in the URL (/tunnels/<TUNNEL_ID>).
settings.cf_tunnel_step3_title: 3. Create an API Token with Read permission:
settings.cf_tunnel_step3_desc: In Cloudflare Dashboard, click your profile in the top-right corner -> My Profile -> API Tokens -> Create Token:
settings.cf_tunnel_step3_item1: Scroll to the bottom and click Create Custom Token.
settings.cf_tunnel_step3_item2: Token name: e.g. StatusPage - Tunnel Reader.
settings.cf_tunnel_step3_item3: Permissions: Add Account > Cloudflare Tunnel > Read.
settings.cf_tunnel_step3_item4: Account Resources: Set Include > All accounts (or select your specific account).
settings.cf_tunnel_step3_item5: Click Continue to summary -> Create Token.
settings.cf_tunnel_step3_item6: Copy the generated secret token and paste it into the Cloudflare API Token field below.
settings.cf_tunnel_step4_desc: Keep "Place in Core Systems" checked if tunnel downtime should mark the global status banner as Major Outage. If disabled, it will be placed as a secondary service under the Cloudflare group.
settings.cf_api_token_help: Requires Account > Cloudflare Tunnel > Read permissions.
settings.cf_worker_desc: Run multi-location latency probes from Cloudflare edge and monitor server downtime autonomously.
settings.cf_worker_guide_title: How to setup your Cloudflare Worker:
settings.cf_worker_step1: Get the template code: Open the local file edge/cloudflare-worker.js in your repository.
settings.cf_worker_step2: Create the Worker: In Cloudflare Dashboard -> Workers & Pages -> Create Application -> Create Worker, and paste the code from edge/cloudflare-worker.js.
settings.cf_worker_var_secret: SHARED_SECRET_TOKEN: A custom password/token (must match the token entered below).
settings.cf_worker_var_discord: DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL: (Optional) Discord webhook for alerts if your origin server dies.
settings.cf_worker_step4: Enable Cron Trigger (Worker Settings -> Triggers -> Cron Triggers): Add * * * * * (every minute) so Cloudflare monitors your server even if your VPS crashes.
settings.cf_worker_step5: Paste URL & Token below: Copy your https://your-worker.workers.dev address into the field below.
settings.cf_worker_url_help: The public .workers.dev endpoint of your deployed worker.
settings.cf_worker_token_help: Used to authenticate requests between your server and the Cloudflare Worker.
